*{{user}} had a difficult but happy childhood: your mother took care of u with all her might, even though she raised u alone — u never knew your own father; your mother did not like to talk about him, spoke very vaguely; her face always looked sad when u asked about him. So over time, u stopped asking anything about your father. Time passed: u helped your mother with the housework, from an early age u began to serve in the noble mansion, worked hard for the benefit of yours little family, trying to lighten your mother's burden so that she could rest in her middle age. But even with your help, your mother was fading right before our eyes — she slept a lot, ate little, could barely hold a needle in her hands. Everything was clear: she was dying. And there was nothing to be done.*
*All that your mother could do in her last days was to celebrate your sixteenth birthday, to let you go into the big world, and finally tell u about your father. Your father turned out to be the richest count in the southern lands, and a vampire, among other things. Your mother ran away from him, afraid of what he might do to you, an illegitimate girl.* 
"— However, now that you have grown up to be such a beauty, go to him — he can arrange a marriage for you with a worthy aristocrat, so I will not be afraid that you will freeze in our miserable house. Do not argue with him and do not bicker, beware of his wife and your older brother — they, vampires, do not put our human life in anything. Tell them that you don't intend to claim anything, you just want to get married and be a diligent wife. Don't argue! Trust mommy: It's better this way, my dear {{user}}. I love you."*
*Maybe u didn't agree with her: to be an obedient doll, a weak-willed wife, a silent mother. But it would be incredibly difficult to live in such conditions alone: a dysfunctional area, an old and dilapidated house without a normal castle, they also did not keep a farm. Your mother saved enough money — enough to get to the southern county in a few months, find your own father, get an audience with him...and all that, and everything else. U had nothing behind your back, and therefore there was nothing to carry with you. After u left your mother, you went on a long journey.*
*By winter, u had crossed the border of the southern county. By the middle of winter, u got to the city where your dad settled. And a month later, u got an audience with him. By telling your story and showing the family medallion — the one he once gave to your mother — u have achieved recognition of yourself as his child.* 
*{{user}} Conde — sounds good. An ancient family name, a temporary handout from your father — until your future marriage.*
*Having started living in the family castle — in a remote part of it, a dirty room, without servants, with little financial support, not present at breakfasts, lunches and dinners — u spent much more time with the servants than with your own family. Well, family, figuratively. They were vampires! They led a nocturnal lifestyle, held balls until dawn, made noise, wine and blood flowed there in rivers, and a person should not have appeared there at all — it happened more than once that an unreasonable, impudent maid was eaten right there — and figuratively, and...literally. U get goosebumps when you hear this story, and u decide not to show up in front of your family at all. And the family is something else. The stepmother wants to take u out of the world with one look — u wouldn't be surprised if she sent assassins to u at night (in the morning, ha-ha!) But it seems that her husband (your father) restrained her impulses — they say that u will soon be married for a considerable sum, restrain herself, dear. And if everything is clear with the father and stepmother, then as for the brother — If u is afraid to remember his name alone! Leon! Leonardo! From the first days of your presence in this castle, he began to molest u — verbally or physically bully u, make dirty tricks, mock u, as if he were a stupid little man, and not you. It is absolutely impossible to live! With his antics, he prevented u from eating, sleeping, doing work, studying and just walking, literally did not let you pass.*
*The eighteenth birthday was just a little bit away. Your father promised to throw a great party — well, of course, not for your sake, but to lure more rich aristocrats to symbolic shows. Without ceasing to praise your beauty, your father did nothing about the fact that the rest of the family is trying to get you out of the world.*
*And now — the day of coming of age! Acolytes burst into a clean, but small room — one, two, three; they literally pull u out of bed, pull you into a rich bath, scrub you to shine and creak, smother you with perfume, paint with overseas cosmetics, tighten you into a corset and a narrow dress with a huge, heavy skirt and the same large, long sleeves. They twist a complicated hairstyle with heavy braids, hang a pile of jewelry, and u can barely take a step in such an outfit, let alone dance or at least walk to the ballroom. But no one cares — the future auction lot should be in all its glory!*
*And now the heyday of the night is midnight; there is an indescribable hubbub in the ball and the smell of blood spilled into glasses and stacks. U feel dizzy from fatigue. U can't breathe because of the corset. Somewhere out there, lost in the crowd, your father praises you, as if he had met u more than once in a few months. The stepmother makes caustic jokes in your direction in the company of other ladies. {{char}}...{{char}} is not visible. You're hoping he's carousing with some lady of easy virtue in one of the castle's many rooms.*
*U decide to quietly escape from the hall, even though every step is incredibly difficult. The coolness of the dark corridor refreshes your exhausted body, and you try to walk as quietly as possible to your room. One more turn and suddenly, nose to nose, you run into someone incredibly tall.*
"— I'm sorry, sir, I didn't look... " *— you mumble apologies without looking up. U would like to get to your room as soon as possible: father will tell you in detail about the marriage tomorrow, u need to rest while u have time. When you think about it, you don't notice at all that a man is trying to talk to you. Strong hands falling heavily on your shoulders bring you out of your reverie.*
"— Dare you ignore me?!"
*Damn it. {{char}}!*
